> 含德之厚，比於赤子。毒蟲不螫，猛獸不據，攫鳥不搏.

Chapter 54 was about 建 and 抱 — actively establishing, actively cradling.

Chapter 55 points the camera at someone who does not know either word: a newborn.

Three characters in the chapter are all actions, and all three are precise.

## 含 is to hold in the mouth

含: 嗛也 — to keep something between the lips. Not hidden in the heart; held in the mouth, neither swallowed nor spat out.

So 含德之厚 is not "possessing a thick store of virtue." It is the state of holding it where it neither has to be consumed nor displayed.

## 握 is to clamp

握: 搤持也 — to grip, to clamp down.

The newborn's fist: 骨弱筋柔而握固. Bones weak, tendons soft, and the grip firm. The thumb is folded inside the fingers — the grip that adults cannot reproduce without effort.

The chapter is intrigued by exactly this: the strength that comes from not having developed.

## 終日號而不嗄

Cries all day and does not go hoarse. 嗄 is the rasp of a throat worn out.

和之至也 — the harmony has reached its limit.

The mechanism is physical: an infant's cry is not forced. The sound comes from an open throat, without the tension of trying to be heard. Adults lose their voices because producing sound involves pushing.

## 未知牝牡之合而朘作，精之至也

Does not yet know the pairing of male and female, and the organ stirs. 精之至 — the essence has reached its limit.

The point is the same in all three cases: the function operates without the intention that adults would use to operate it. Nothing is being summoned; it is simply there.

## 知和曰常，知常曰明

Knowing 和 is called 常; knowing 常 is called 明.

Same 常 and 明 as chapter 16. The 常 is the invariant; 明 is the light that comes from seeing it.

Here the invariant is identified as 和 — harmony, the state in which the parts are not forcing each other. Which is chapter 42's 沖氣以為和 arriving as a description of a body.

## 益生曰祥

祥: 福也 — but in the pre-Qin period it is used both ways: auspicious is 祥, and ominous is also 祥. It means omen.

So 益生曰祥 is not "adding to life is good." It is: deliberately adding to life is a sign — a portent, and not necessarily a favorable one.

Which is exactly chapter 50's 生生之厚: the effort to add to life is itself the omen.

## 心使氣曰強

使: 伶也 — to dispatch a person to do a job.

心使氣 — the mind dispatches the breath to do work. That is 強: not strength, but the strain of a command being issued to something that should be running on its own.

## 物壯則老，謂之不道

A thing at its peak ages; this is called not-the-way. Not-the-way ends early.

The line is the same as chapter 30's, and here it lands differently: the peak is what happens when the summoning succeeds. Every 強 is a peak, and every peak has already begun to age.

## The two motions

The infant holds the fist inward and keeps the milk in the mouth.
The adult sends the breath outward and feeds the body outward.

That is the chapter's dividing line, and it is anatomical rather than moral: the infant's default is retention; the adult's default is dispatch.
